about: HAND-KEPT: for each name that can print an `[icraft.live] FIRED` line, the action that makes it fire. `node --expose-internals dev/loud/gen_liveness.js --sheet <file>` joins this with the scripts and writes the in-game check sheet (kept in the internal repo: dev/liveness-check-sheet.md). The scripted checks of the test PC run these actions and assert the lines.

`features`: one entry per icraft.live.fired name (the generator refuses a sheet with a feature that has none): `proves` = what the line means, `do` = the instruction, `cmd` = paste-ready commands in order, `needs` = what must be true first. `<Name>` is the test player.

`events`: the action for every handler of an event that has no entry of its own. `ids`: an entry for one id (<name>@<group>). The generator adds what it reads from the script itself: the item a handler is registered for, a tick function's interval, who a hurt handler listens to.
Ids are the ones the scripts and registries use; look one up before writing it. No player names: this file is public.

abyssal-artifact.proves: the artifact rule's chance passed on a real roll and one artifact was added (a LootJS rule has no script code at roll time; the rule carries one action for this line)
abyssal-artifact.do: Roll the Nightblade's kill loot (its chance is 100%; Elder and The Roka share the line at lower chances).

ascension-status.proves: the status command read the world's Ascension level and answered
ascension-status.do: Say `!ascension` in chat; expect "This world is at base difficulty (Ascension 0)." Do NOT set a level above 0 on the live world.

boss-x3.proves: a boss of the roster was given the x3 through core.spawnBuff (saved modifiers)
boss-x3.do: Summon a roster boss, then read its modifiers (icraft_boss_3x_hp under max health).

codex-balance.proves: the balance scan SAW tokens in an inventory (its loop ran zero times until 2026-10-12)
codex-balance.do: Hold a token, ask for the balance; the line for Tier 1 reads 1 / 500.

codex-exchange.proves: tokens were found, taken and paid out as XP
codex-exchange.needs: the player holds the stage tier_4 (the exchange is closed below it)

codex-submit.proves: a submission scanned the inventory, took materials and granted tokens (its loops ran zero times until 2026-10-12)
codex-submit.do: Submit 100 iron ingots: 1 token of the player's current tier, the ingots are gone.
codex-submit.needs: the player is below tier_4 (bulk metals stop minting at the last tier) and under the iron cap

compass-of-return.proves: the teleport command moved the player (the compass never teleported anyone before 2026-10-11)
compass-of-return.do: Right-click a bed (that sets the point), walk away, right-click the compass; expect "The needle guides you home."

first-kill-book.proves: a first-kill reward of an Iron's Spellbooks boss was dropped at the boss
first-kill-book.do: Kill one of the four bosses as a player for the first time (the damage command gives the kill to the player).
first-kill-book.needs: a player who has not had this boss's first-kill reward

quest-bridge.proves: a Heracles dummy completed its quest (the Level Up bridge: quest onboarding_first_level)
quest-bridge.do: Raise any aptitude to level 2; the quest "Level Up" completes a few seconds later.
quest-bridge.needs: a player whose quest "Level Up" is unlocked and not complete

relic-sink.proves: the sweep found relics in the backpack, took them and paid essence (its loops ran zero times until 2026-10-12)
relic-sink.do: Convert one curio: the preview lists it, the confirm takes it and gives 20 Relic Essence.

relic-sink-deny.proves: the deny list denied a carried item (it matched nothing until 2026-10-12: a Set asked with a Java string)
relic-sink-deny.do: Carry a deny-listed item and ask for the preview: the item is not offered.

skill-craft-bonus.proves: Craft Bonus rolled on a real craft and handed the copy out (it rolled on every inventory change before 2026-10-12)
skill-craft-bonus.do: With the score at 100, craft sticks from planks in survival: one extra stick is given. Then set the score back.
skill-craft-bonus.needs: survival mode (the handler skips creative and spectator)

skill-material-save.proves: Material Save rolled on a real craft and handed its material out (it rolled on every inventory change before 2026-10-12)
skill-material-save.do: With the score at 100, craft an iron pickaxe in survival: an iron ingot or nugget is given. Then set the score back.
skill-material-save.needs: survival mode (the handler skips creative and spectator)

spawn-buff-repaired.proves: a mob saved before 2026-10-12 without its buff got it back as saved modifiers, and kept its share of health
spawn-buff-repaired.do: Walk to a boss or scaled mob that was saved in the world before 2026-10-12 (its chunk must load).
spawn-buff-repaired.needs: such a mob exists: on a fresh world this line cannot appear

spawn-buff-saved.proves: a fresh mob got its spawn buff as SAVED modifiers (they were lost on every save before 2026-10-12)
spawn-buff-saved.do: Nothing: the first scaled mob that spawns fires it, usually before anyone joins.

unique-bow-effects.proves: an arrow tagged by a unique bow hit a living victim and the bow's effect code was reached (it returned on every hit until 2026-10-11)
unique-bow-effects.do: Shoot a mob with the bow: Blindness and Weakness on the victim.

unique-tier-buff.proves: a hit with a unique weapon (or its tagged arrow) was multiplied by its tier (inert until 2026-10-11)
unique-tier-buff.do: Hit a mob with the sword.

wither-relic.proves: the Wither's Dormant Relic was dropped at the boss (guaranteed on a player's first kill, 15% after)
wither-relic.do: Kill a Wither as a player; simplyswords:dormant_relic drops where it dies, after its dying animation.
cmd: (wait 11 seconds: the Wither is invulnerable while it charges up)
wither-relic.needs: a player who has not had the Wither's first-kill reward (otherwise about 1 kill in 7). CONFIRMED 2026-10-13 on full-pack boots: the Wither a player fights is `progressivebosses:wither` (Progressive Bosses replaces every `minecraft:wither` the moment it spawns, summoned or built), and the boss registry makes it the Wither for every rule. So the selectors name that type; `type=minecraft:wither` finds nothing. The replacement ignores `{NoAI:1b}`: it is a real, attacking Wither. It is invulnerable for its first 11 seconds (`/damage` does nothing until then), and after the killing hit it plays a 5-second dying animation (measured: 100 of its ticks) and only then drops its loot; by the mod's data it explodes at the end (power 8, not observed): stand back, away from anything you want to keep, and away from the world spawn (the spawn village deletes hostile mobs).

wither-tablets.proves: the Wither's loot rule ran on a real roll (2 simplyswords:runic_tablet each time; the rule carries one action for this line)
wither-tablets.do: Roll the Wither's kill loot: 2 Runic Tablets every time.
wither-tablets.needs: nothing but the Wither: the loot command rolls its kill loot without a fight (measured: 2 Runic Tablets in 40 of 40 rolls). `/kill` was not tried on this entity: expect it to die like a killed one (below). CONFIRMED 2026-10-13 on full-pack boots: the Wither a player fights is `progressivebosses:wither` (Progressive Bosses replaces every `minecraft:wither` the moment it spawns, summoned or built), and the boss registry makes it the Wither for every rule. So the selectors name that type; `type=minecraft:wither` finds nothing. The replacement ignores `{NoAI:1b}`: it is a real, attacking Wither. It is invulnerable for its first 11 seconds (`/damage` does nothing until then), and after the killing hit it plays a 5-second dying animation (measured: 100 of its ticks) and only then drops its loot; by the mod's data it explodes at the end (power 8, not observed): stand back, away from anything you want to keep, and away from the world spawn (the spawn village deletes hostile mobs).

vorpal-decap.proves: a critical melee hit with Vorpal passed its roll and was made lethal (the mob dies at once and may drop its head)
vorpal-decap.do: Critical hits (falling) on non-boss mobs with a sword enchanted ensorcellation:vorpal: 5% per level a hit, so about 1 in 4 crits at level 5.
vorpal-decap.needs: survival or adventure reach, and a real critical hit (the handler reads the crit stamp attribute_sync.js writes)

arcane-decap.proves: a critical spell hit with Arcane Vorpal passed its roll and was made lethal
arcane-decap.do: Critical spell hits on non-boss mobs with a staff or spellbook enchanted iridescent_reforging:vorpal_arcane.
arcane-decap.needs: a caster with spell crit chance; the roll is per level, as for Vorpal

per-kill-counted.proves: a boss with the registry flag perKill died and every player within 64 blocks had one kill added to their own count
per-kill-counted.do: More than 100 blocks from the world spawn, summon a flagged boss and kill it within 64 blocks; then `/icraft bosskills` lists 1 kill.

per-kill-scaled.proves: a flagged boss traded its first hit with a player whose count is 1 or more, and was fixed above base (saved modifiers icraft_pk_hp / _dmg / _spd, one chat line)
per-kill-scaled.do: After the kill of per-kill-counted, summon the same boss and hit it once: the chat line says fight 2, +15 % health, +10 % damage, +3 % speed.
per-kill-scaled.needs: per-kill-counted done by the same player

groups.tick.player: a player tick function runs for each online player when `player.age % interval == offset`: be online for at most `interval` ticks
groups.tick.server: a server tick function runs with nobody online, when `tick % interval == offset`: it fires by itself within `interval` ticks of the load
groups.hurt: a handler of the shared hurt dispatcher (0_lib_core.js): it fires on the first hit it listens to whose gate is open and that it survives
groups.hurt.late: the same, in the LATE phase (after every script's normal handlers)

events.AStageEvents.added: Give the test player a stage they do not have (a tier is granted by its trigger: a boss kill or a Codex submission).
events.BlockEvents.rightClicked: Right-click any block (a bed for the Compass of Return).
events.EntityEvents.checkSpawn: Nothing: any natural spawn attempt near a player fires it. Stand in the dark for a minute.

EntityEvents.death.do: Kill any mob as a player.

events.EntityEvents.spawned: Nothing: the first mob that spawns fires it, usually before anyone joins.
events.ItemEvents.canPickUp: Drop an item and walk over it.
events.ItemEvents.crafted: Craft anything in survival (planks into sticks).
events.ItemEvents.entityInteracted: Right-click any mob with an item in hand.
events.ItemEvents.pickedUp: Drop an item and pick it up again.
events.ItemEvents.tooltip: On the CLIENT (logs/kubejs/client.log): open the inventory and hover an item; the handler runs when the game first builds tooltips.
events.JEIEvents.hideItems: On the CLIENT (logs/kubejs/client.log): join a world; JEI runs the handler when it loads its plugins.
events.ItemEvents.rightClicked: Right-click with the item the handler is registered for (the column names it when the script writes it as a literal; otherwise any item).
events.PlayerEvents.inventoryChanged: Pick up or move any item.
events.PlayerEvents.loggedOut: Leave the server (the line is printed after the player is gone).
events.ServerEvents.unloaded: Nothing: it fires when the server stops; the line is among the last of the log.
